claude_subscription.note: The lane discriminator is ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, never the model id. A native subscription session legitimately reports a `[1m]` model id; that suffix is a context-window marker.

ica_gateway_messages_shim.note: Azure-backed GPT deployments on the gateway reject Claude Code's output_config; this lane is the local param-strip proxy in front of the same shared gateway. Same sovereignty.

ica_gateway_responses_shim.note: Codex driven against a LOCAL shim that fronts the SHARED gateway. The local hop does not make it local: the tokens are still served by the third-party shared pool. This row is the concrete case invariant 2 exists for.

codex_subscription.note: Personal ChatGPT subscription execution. Account identity is explicit and orthogonal to provider, model, effort and task role. Secondary is the agentic default; Primary is an equally eligible explicit alternative. Unavailable accounts return a routing fact; a new routing decision names the next account, without silent replay or rotation.

gemini_direct.probe: UNCONFIRMED, same shape as codex_subscription: a direct metered API key on an account we control, not a seat. No class currently declares a floor that would route here, so the classification is not yet load-bearing. Ask Nick alongside codex.

bob_ibm_shell.probe: DELIBERATELY UNCLASSIFIED — the evidence contradicts itself and `unknown` clears no floor, which is the fail-closed answer. The registry entry says `family: local` / `allowance: local`, but the `bob-shell-delegate` skill describes it as the IBM Bob Shell CLI, i.e. IBM-hosted. `allowance: local` most likely means "a locally-run CLI binary", which is a statement about where the PROCESS runs, not where INFERENCE runs — and inference is what sovereignty is about. PROBE: run `bob` with the network down, or inspect ~/.config/bob* for a gateway URL + credential. Do not classify it from the `allowance` field.

nano_banana_api.probe: Never classified; has no branch in buildRegistryInvocation() either. No floored class routes to image generation today, so `unknown` costs nothing and asserts nothing.

sora_api.probe: Same as nano_banana_api — unclassified, and no floored class reaches it.

external_candidate.probe: Shared lane for the M5b external-provider candidates below (deepseek-v4-flash, qwen3-flash, kimi-k2, glm, grok) — all `status: candidate`, `enabled: false`, `executor_status: absent`. claude-opus-5-5.descriptor: Claude Opus 5.5 (released 2026-09-22) — the AOS SPINE / MUST-stay tier as of 2026-09-22 (orchestration, verdict/adjudication, final synthesis, architecture, mode-d, schema-recovery, cross-wave merge; agentic_meta_dev CLAUDE.md 'Model × provider × effort'), superseding claude-opus-5 (kept selectable as the legacy/fallback chain entry — reconciled node_01M3F4F5G93P21P1WAH565MAYQ 2026-09-27). Exact API ID claude-opus-5-5; Anthropic documents 1M context, 128K maximum output, adaptive thinking always on, and $4/$20 per input/output MTok ($0.20 cache reads). Anthropic reports >30% faster output than Opus 5 and recommends starting most workloads here, escalating to Fable 5.1 after higher-effort Opus 5.5 falls short. Those routing/performance claims are vendor-reported, not locally measured. Harness caveat MEASURED FROM PRIMARY: preserved thinking applies to API accounts created on/after 2026-08-31, so prior Claude context cannot be edited. Forced-tool-choice and thinking-history behavior are UNKNOWN. ICA ccx Claude-Code wrapper smoke 2026-09-24: claude-opus-5-5[1m] rc 0, canonicalModel claude-opus-5-5, contextWindow 1000000; raw-HTTP bare-id behavior was not re-measured. claude-opus-5.descriptor: Claude Opus 5 (released 2026-07-24) — LEGACY as of 2026-09-22 (superseded by claude-opus-5-5 as the AOS SPINE / MUST-stay tier — orchestration, verdict/adjudication, final synthesis, architecture, mode-d, schema-recovery, cross-wave merge; reconciled node_01M3F4F5G93P21P1WAH565MAYQ 2026-09-27). Still selectable, and kept as the in-chain legacy/fallback entry behind claude-opus-5-5 for orchestration/mode_d. Supersedes Opus 4.8 (now legacy): same price ($5/$25 per M), >2x Opus 4.8's agentic performance at a lower cost per task, per Anthropic 'start here for complex agentic coding and enterprise work' (that guidance predates the Opus 5.5 launch). 1M context, 128K max output; adaptive thinking; effort defaults to `high` on the Claude API + Claude Code (set explicitly to change). New tokenizer (same ~30%-heavier family as Opus 4.7+/Sonnet 5). Knowledge cutoff May 2026. Trails Fable 5 but surpasses Opus 4.8. ICA: SERVABLE + VERIFIED 2026-07-31 — claude-opus-5[1m] was the ICA spine-offload lane and is now the fallback behind claude-opus-5-5[1m] (claude-opus-4-8[1m] = older fallback). On the ICA lane: 1M ctx via the [1m] id (plain id caps at 200k), maxOutputTokens reported 64,000 (ICA-side cap, below the 128K first-party ceiling), tool_use + adaptive thinking (output_config.effort) + legacy thinking.type:enabled + output_config.format (structured JSON) ALL work — Opus 5 has no structured-output gap on ICA, unlike Sonnet 5.

claude-opus-4-8.descriptor: Claude Opus 4.8 — LEGACY as of 2026-07-24 (superseded by claude-opus-5 as the spine; Anthropic moved it to the legacy model list). Still selectable, and still an ICA [1m] lane — but as of 2026-07-31 it is the spine-offload FALLBACK, not the primary: ICA now serves claude-opus-5[1m] (verified), which takes the lane. Deep reasoning, orchestration, architecture. $5/$25 per M, 1M context, 128K max output.

claude-opus-4-7.descriptor: Opus 4.7 — stronger reasoning than 4.6. Available via ICA (shared pool).

claude-opus-4-6.descriptor: Opus 4.6 — deep reasoning, architecture decisions. Available via ICA (shared pool).

claude-sonnet-5-5.descriptor: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (released 2026-09-28, https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5). Default subscription/native-execution Sonnet for CONTRACT-CLEAR execution/review/research, superseding claude-sonnet-5 (Nick, 2026-09-28) — NOT a blanket default: `design_judgment` (architecture/UX-visual-design/hard-judgment/ambiguous-synthesis) and `raw_strength` (hard-algorithmic/debugging/reasoning-heavy) are separate task classes that never resolve here (Nick, 2026-09-28 evening; see the routing_policy chains above). Adaptive thinking; default effort `high` on the raw API but Claude Code itself defaults it to Medium; extended-thinking params (thinking.type:enabled + budget_tokens) NOT accepted — adaptive-only. Sourced from platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview (authoritative for id/pricing/limits) + the announcement page for benchmarks: 1M context, 128K output (300K via Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header). $2/$10 per MTok — same headline price as Sonnet 5 — plus cache read $0.20/MTok, cache write $2.50/MTok; Anthropic claims 30%+ faster output and up to 30% lower cost-per-task vs Sonnet 5 via token efficiency. Benchmarks (self-reported announcement page, Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5): Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.6%/10.3%/66.4%; FrontierCode 1.1 (Main, Max effort) 46.2%/42.4%/54.4%; CursorBench 4.0 55.5%/34.1%/57.8%; OSWorld 2.1 (partial) 80.1%/57.0%/81.8%; GDPval-AA v2.1 1844/1449/1846; Chartography (no tools) 61.6%/15.6%/64.4% — beats Sonnet 5 on every listed benchmark and sits close to Opus 5.5 (within a few points on several) at half its per-MTok price. Local Claude Code probe (2026-09-28): `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 'reply ok'` → stderr `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]` (benign, per the `unrecognized-model-stderr-is-benign` lesson) + stdout `ok`, exit 0 — this harness accepts the id. ⚠️ ICA does NOT yet serve Sonnet 5.5 as of 2026-09-28 (same shape as the Codex-subscription/ICA GPT-5.6 split) — the ICA Sonnet offload lane stays `claude-sonnet-5[1m]` until ICA adds it, and until then ICA's preferred Claude model is `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` (see that model's ICA provider row), not Sonnet 5. Tracker `node_01M3MWZ6564YV32VCMMGAV5DN2` (tree tree_01KVTH95ETM8YRYCV2ENHVR124, 'Update ICA Sonnet mapping to 5.5 when ICA serves it'); probe = a bare-id HTTP 200 check against the ICA gateway (see `ica-ccx-bare-ids-only` lesson) with model_id `claude-sonnet-5-5` (not `[1m]`).

claude-sonnet-5.descriptor: Claude Sonnet 5 (released 2026-06-30). LEGACY BUT SELECTABLE as of 2026-09-28 — claude-sonnet-5-5 is now the default subscription/native-execution Sonnet (see that entry above); Sonnet 5 stays the live ICA offload lane (`claude-sonnet-5[1m]`, shared pool) since ICA does not yet serve 5.5. Near-Opus coding/agentic quality at Sonnet cost. Adaptive thinking on by default (native path); first Sonnet with xhigh effort; new tokenizer (~30% more tokens vs 4.6). $2/$10 per M — the 2026-06-30 intro price is now Anthropic's standard price; the previously-scheduled 2026-09-01 increase to $3/$15 did NOT occur (verified against the live Claude/Anthropic pricing page, retrieved 2026-09-27: $2/$10, cache read $0.20/MTok, no intro-pricing disclaimer; corroborates node_01M3HW1ECPSXFCREDCKC6R8FE4, reconciled 2026-09-27). ALSO on ICA (shared pool) since 2026-07-08 via claude-sonnet-5[1m] (1M) — the current-gen free-offload lane, superseding ICA Sonnet 4.6. 1M context, 128K output. ✅ ICA path reasoning REVALIDATED WORKING (2026-07-20, supersedes the stale 2026-07-09 no-op finding): Claude Code (2.1.215) now emits thinking.type:adaptive + output_config.effort → ICA Sonnet 5 reasons end-to-end (adaptive + effort scaling honored; legacy thinking.type:enabled now 400s). Reasoning-dependent legs MAY offload to ica/claude-sonnet-5[1m] behind a reviewer gate. ⚠️ One gap: output_config.format (structured-JSON schema) is silently dropped by the ICA gateway → prose not schema JSON; use a forced tool-call for structured output on the ICA lane.
claude-sonnet-5.reasoning_caveat: ICA offload lane (ica/claude-sonnet-5[1m]) reasoning WORKS via Claude Code (revalidated 2026-07-20 — supersedes the 2026-07-09 no-op finding): adaptive thinking + output_config.effort honored end-to-end. Reasoning-dependent offload is fine here. Only remaining gap: output_config.format (structured JSON) is dropped by the gateway — use a tool-call for structured output.
claude-sonnet-5.token_economy_note: Sonnet 5's new tokenizer emits ~30% more tokens than Sonnet 4.6 for the same text, so its EFFECTIVE metered cost is ~$2.60/$13.00-equivalent at the now-standard $2/$10 price (the scheduled rise to $3/$15 did not occur — see descriptor, reconciled 2026-09-27). HEAD-TO-HEAD RUN 2026-08-26 (node_01M0Z7K4QJXD2EWK0BPKD98QVG, n=3 prompts per use case, one operator/session, same ICA ccx /v1/messages transport for both models — see docs/audits/gemini-3.7-vs-3.6-flash-head-to-head-2026-08-26.md in agentic_meta_dev): gemini-3.7-flash matched-or-beat gemini-3.6-flash on every one of 9 prompts (web-research synthesis, second-opinion code/reasoning/SQL critique, SVG icon generation) AND consumed meaningfully fewer output tokens per completion at matched max_tokens budgets — 3.6-flash was truncated mid-answer on 5 of 9 prompts at budgets where 3.7-flash completed cleanly (one SVG prompt needed a 10,000-token budget for 3.6-flash to finish vs 4,471 for 3.7-flash on the same prompt), and 3.6-flash also broke an explicit 'no markdown fences' instruction on one SVG prompt where 3.7-flash complied. RECOMMENDATION: promote to a leg-1/leg-2 ICA-only entry in second_opinion and svg_generation ahead of gemini-3.6-flash's ICA rows, and to web_research's ICA fallback leg (native gemini-3.6-flash stays leg-1 there since it alone has Search grounding) — pending human review of the pilot before flipping enabled/routing_policy. Still NOT auto-routed (n=3 pilot, single session, no adversarial verification of its own scoring).

mistral-medium-2505.descriptor: Mistral Medium 2505 — the first Mistral model on any ICA lane, discovered on the ccx catalog 2026-08-26. Tool use + structured output OK; watsonx-backed, so emits tool-call arguments as a JSON string — call it on /v1/chat/completions, never /v1/messages (the Anthropic-shape translation layer 500s on the string form).

nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super.descriptor: NVIDIA Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B (v1.5 served) on the ICA ccx gateway — discovered and bench-evaluated 2026-10-07 (node_01M4C0PWMG1922F4HQ0TPWZVTG; probe+bench receipt docs/project_plans/reports/model-eval/nemotron-super-2026-10-07/ in agentic_meta_dev). Wire id: bare `nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super` ([1m] suffix 403s). Context window: 131,072 tokens. Economics: FREE (x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0). Always-on thinking: the model cannot suppress its chain-of-thought — it always emits reasoning before answering, and on complex tasks the thinking trace leaks into text output (bench T2: leaked ~500-token reasoning trace instead of a clean single-word answer). Tool-use: the model responds to tool declarations but uses a custom <TOOLCALL> XML format, NOT standard Anthropic tool_use blocks or OpenAI function_call/tool_calls — incompatible with AOS infrastructure. Latency: avg ~6s (vs Haiku ~1.8s, GPT-luna ~2.7s) due to always-on thinking. Transport: both /chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible) and /v1/messages (Anthropic-compatible) return 200 on bare id. Bench verdict: correct on extraction/code-fix/summarization/JSON-schema tasks; format failure on classification (T2); registered not routed. Positioning bench 2026-10-07 (node_01M4C58QYW0KP7987JWADP8YKV): earns NO role. The Codex harness rejected it (400, so no agentic arm), it returned empty text on a 102K-token retrieval, and two of five short tasks failed format (an empty triage reply, an unparseable schema reply). It was also the slowest arm (24-44 s). AA Intelligence Index ~9 (estimated; AA marks it deprecated).

providers.capability_gap: tool-use emits custom <TOOLCALL> XML (not standard Anthropic tool_use or OpenAI tool_calls); thinking traces leak into text output on multi-step judgment tasks
